rationale: Round-8 zero-ask regression check of 2e73a0f3 under the grounding lens. SEAM AUDIT (G2): the claim 'chunk 6 already carried the executor files (checked, not assumed)' is TRUE — internal/executor/executor.go, mindspec_executor.go, and mock.go are all in chunk 6's key_file_paths (and have been since 747bf9b3). The seven named seam methods (SnapshotWorktreeTree, MaterializeStageCommit, PublishStageMarker, ReadStageMarker, ClearStageMarker, AdvanceBranchExpectedOld, ResetIndexToHead) plus ChangedFilesTree collide with NOTHING in internal/executor or internal/gitutil — all genuinely new identifiers on a real interface (Executor at executor.go:19) with a real mock (MockExecutor at mock.go:7). The boundary sentence ('internal/complete calls ONLY these seams and gains no new gitutil import') matches a discipline the package already documents about itself: internal/complete has zero non-comment gitutil imports today, and panel_advisory.go:94-96 states the no-direct-gitutil-import seam-routing rule explicitly — so the ADR-0030 conformance claim is grounded in existing practice, not aspiration. IDEMPOTENCE PREMISES (G1): three of four verify cleanly. R's mixed reset as a state-function of (tip, worktree), index-only — lab-verified in my rounds 5/6. S's export as a deterministic projection — ADR-0025's OWN text, verbatim: ':15 a deterministic projection: bd export rewrites it from the current Dolt rows' and ':19 given Dolt state at time T, bd export produces byte-identical output every time'; the forward-correct-for-a-cache framing under changed Dolt state is a fair extension of the same decision item. The merge premise rides the 127 convergence machinery verified in rounds 2-4 (merge_resumption.go, CommitTreeMerge, preserved-merge resume). The elided-transition-graph completion is coherent with my round-7 CREATE lab (CREATE semantics are value-agnostic, so absent→D parenting on A behaves identically to absent→C), and the both-elided no-marker route is sound (no ref movement, tip still at reviewed SHA, ordinary re-entry). The at-least-once contract choice itself is honest engineering — the round-6 exactly-once claim IS unprovable after a post-no-op-S kill, and the withdrawal is stated in place rather than silently edited, which is the evidence discipline this panel exists to enforce. ONE minor precision defect, NOT implementation-corrupting: the fourth premise — 'S's dirt classification is a pure read + refusal' — is inaccurate about the classifier the plan names. The S-exit contract says 'the existing artifact/user classifier', and that function, next.CheckDirtyTreeDetail (guard.go:336-357), is only conditionally pure: when artifact dirt is present it calls exportBeadsFn(repoRoot) — a worktree WRITE to .beads/issues.jsonl — then re-classifies (guard.go:347-355). On the S-exit path the artifact should be clean (S just committed the fresh projection), so the write branch fires only if Dolt changed mid-run, and even then the write is the same deterministic projection the S-export proof already covers — replay still converges, so the at-least-once contract HOLDS; only the 'pure read' label is wrong for the named entry point. Bead 6 should either call the pure classification core (classifyDirty over status, without the normalization branch) or restate the premise as 'read + idempotent normalization per the S-export proof'. One clause; recording as minor for fold-in, not blocking at the round-8 bar.

findings.evidence: The S-exit contract names 'the existing artifact/user classifier'; next.CheckDirtyTreeDetail (internal/next/guard.go:336-357) writes the worktree on its artifact-dirt branch (exportBeadsFn at :347 — bd export normalization) before re-classifying.
